sections.title: ISO 12944 corrosivity categories — marine + offshore qualification

dataHighlight.heading: Marine + offshore corrosivity demand durability class H or VH coatings + NORSOK M-501
dataHighlight.text: ISO 12944-2 categorises atmospheric corrosivity on a six-step scale: C1 indoor climate-controlled; C2 low (dry indoor unheated); C3 medium (urban / mild industrial); C4 high (industrial / coastal); C5-M high-marine (coastal + offshore near-surface); CX extreme (offshore, subsea splash zone, tropical marine). Marine + offshore deployments require durability class H (15-25 years) or VH (>25 years) coating systems per ISO 12944-5 with paint-system certificates covering primer / intermediate / topcoat dry-film thickness and adhesion. NORSOK M-501 (Surface preparation and protective coating) governs Norwegian Continental Shelf offshore assets; NACE SP0492-2020 governs US field inspection. Proud Tek offshore-rated marine plaques use 316L stainless 2 mm backplate + PTFE gasket + EPDM grommet, certified through ASTM B117 96-500 h salt-spray and ISO 9227 cyclic corrosion across the full ISO 12944 corrosivity range.

sections.title: Operating playbook — outdoor / rugged programmes
paragraphs: Oil & gas upstream + midstream + downstream operators commonly specify ATEX Zone 1 Ex ib IIC T4 + IECEx + NEC Class I Div 1 Group D tags on wellheads, Christmas trees, pigging-launcher stations, manifolds, separators, compressor stations, and refinery unit operations. Corrosion posture lands on ISO 12944 C5-M (coastal refinery) or CX (offshore platform) with 316L through-bolt mounting and NORSOK M-501 + NACE SP0492 qualified coating. Chip selection commonly spans {chip:impinj-m775:name} or {chip:nxp-ucode-9xe:name} with GS1 GIAI-96 individual-asset identifier feeding EPCIS 2.0 into IBM Maximo Oil & Gas, SAP S/4HANA EAM IS-Oil, Oracle EBS eAM, Bentley AssetWise APM, AVEVA PI + APM, and Hexagon EAM.

Offshore wind + renewable operators (Ørsted, Vestas, Siemens Gamesa, GE Renewable Energy, Equinor, RWE) commonly specify ISO 12944 CX + IEC 61400-6 Tower & Foundations + DNV-ST-0126 support-structures qualification. Tag form factors include 316L stainless plaque on tower doors, blade-root anti-metal discs for rotating-component inspection, and nacelle platform tags tied into DNV Nexus + DNV Veracity + Bazefield + Siemens Gamesa Gamesa Digital + Vestas Power Plant Solutions + GE Digital APM (Meridium).

Electric utility + transmission operators commonly specify IP67 + ISO 12944 C3-C4 + NESC + ANSI C2 + ANSI O5.1 (wood pole) tags on distribution poles, transformers, substations, cross-arms, and conductor infrastructure. GIAI-96 + GPS geolocation flows into ESRI ArcGIS GeoBIM, AssetWise, and Oracle Utilities Work & Asset Management; vehicle-mounted + drone-mounted + handheld scan workflows support storm-damage assessment and vegetation-management programmes.

Food & pharma sanitary programmes commonly specify IP69K + FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 elastomer + EHEDG hygienic-design + 3-A Sanitary Standards + USDA-inspected meat / dairy plant wash-down. faq.question: What's the difference between IP67, IP68, and IP69K?
faq.answer: IP67 (IEC 60529) covers temporary immersion to 1 m for 30 min — standard for general outdoor asset tracking. IP68 covers continuous immersion per manufacturer specification, typically 1-3 m for 24-72 h — for flood-prone, underground vault, or near-water permanent installations. IP69K (ISO 20653) covers high-pressure wash-down at 80 °C / 100 bar / 14-16 L·min⁻¹, 30 sec per face from 0 / 30 / 60 / 90° angles — mandatory for food, dairy, meat, and pharma sanitary CIP (clean-in-place) wash-down environments. NEMA 250 equivalents map IP67 → Type 6, IP68 → Type 6P, IP69K → Type 4X wash-down-corrosion-resistant.

faq.question: How do I choose between ATEX, IECEx, and NEC hazardous-area certification?
faq.answer: ATEX (2014/34/EU) is the EU framework; IECEx is the international (33+ member economies) framework; NEC Class / Division is the North American framework. For a hazardous-area installation in the EU, ATEX Zone 1 Ex ib IIC T4 Gb is typical for gas atmospheres (refinery crude distillation, LNG terminal, offshore wellhead). For global deployments, IECEx provides cross-border acceptance. For US + Canada, NEC Class I Division 1 Group B / C / D (gas) + Class II Division 1 (dust) paired with UL 913 intrinsic safety is the standard path. Gas groups IIA (propane) / IIB (ethylene) / IIC (hydrogen, acetylene) reflect the explosive mixture; T-ratings T3 (200 °C) / T4 (135 °C) / T5 (100 °C) / T6 (85 °C) reflect surface-temperature class.

faq.question: What read range do I get with a long-range outdoor UHF tag?
faq.answer: 3-12 m depending on chip, antenna, and environment. {chip:impinj-monza-r6-p:name} delivers 3-6 m cost-optimised. {chip:impinj-m750:name} / M770 delivers 4-8 m with Autotune for dense-metal environments. {chip:impinj-m775:name} delivers 6-12 m with optional RFMicron sensor for vehicle drive-by and yard-management portals. {chip:nxp-ucode-9xe:name} delivers 4-8 m with 128-bit EPC for extended identifier encoding (no user memory on UCODE 9xe per NXP SL3S1216 datasheet); UCODE 9xm is the variant when on-tag user data is needed. {chip:alien-higgs-9:name} delivers 4-8 m with robust wet-RF performance. Read range degrades with wet surfaces, heavy metal environment, and tag-to-reader orientation; Autotune chips compensate for detuning in wet / cold / hot / dense-metal operating conditions.

faq.question: Can the tag be installed directly on metal assets?
faq.answer: Yes — Proud Tek's on-metal SKU uses a PCB antenna with ferrite backing or foam spacer that decouples the radiator from the metal surface, preserving read range. Mounting options include 3M VHB industrial adhesive, 316L stainless M6 / M8 / M10 through-bolt, cable-wrap silicone loop (5-60 mm diameter range), or bolt-mount anchor with PTFE gasket + EPDM grommet (offshore SKU). Non-metal-mount tags installed directly on steel / aluminium / copper lose 70-90 % of read range; always specify whether the asset is metallic when scoping the programme.

faq.question: What identifier should I use — SGTIN, GIAI, or GRAI?
faq.answer: GS1 General Specifications v24 + EPC Tag Data Standard v2.1 define three relevant identifiers. SGTIN-96 (Serialised Global Trade Item Number) carries a GTIN + serial — used for product-level tracking of identical SKU. GIAI-96 (Global Individual Asset Identifier) carries a per-asset serial — used for fixed-asset tracking where every tag is unique (utility pole, pump, wind-turbine blade, wellhead). GRAI-96 (Global Returnable Asset Identifier) carries a returnable-asset serial — used for reusable containers, pallets, cylinders, and rental-fleet equipment. Most outdoor / industrial / energy / utility programmes use GIAI-96; pallet / container / cylinder programmes use GRAI-96; packaged-goods / SKU-level programmes use SGTIN-96.
